# RUN — {Procedure} on {dataset snapshot}

**ID**: `cpt-{system}-run-{slug}`

## Table of Contents

<!-- generated by `cfs toc` -->

<!-- One RUN = one execution of one procedure (a fit, an estimation, a statistical test, an optimisation, a classification, …) on one snapshot of the DATASET, judged against the PLAN criteria. Simulations are acquisition (DATASET); design proposals are phase output; ranking against other candidates is the COMPARISON's job. Keep only headings and {placeholder} text in this file. -->

## 1. Unit

{DATASET ID(s) and the snapshot: which experiments (names, count, total data points = points per experiment × count) and their origin composition ({n} ground-truth, {m} simulated). The COMPARISON this RUN is a candidate in, once it exists: `cpt-{system}-comparison-{slug}`. A RUN on simulated data tests the candidate and the design; a RUN on ground truth tests the system; say which this is. A RUN uses every experiment acquired so far; anything excluded is listed in Deviations with a reason that does not mention the outcome.}

## 2. Procedure

{The procedure and the tool that executes it (fit tool, test, optimiser, classifier, …), its MCP server and contract version. Phase and cycle in which it ran (e.g. POST-1, or CYCLE-1 of cycle 2). Which call of that phase this was, out of the phase limit for that tool.}

## 3. Candidate Spec

{What the procedure was applied with, exactly as the tool consumes it: for a fit, the model spec (states, parameters with finite ranges, initial state, algebraics, right-hand sides, observables); for a test, the hypotheses and the statistic; for an optimisation, objective and constraints. Then the governing equations or decision rule in mathematical form with every symbol named and its unit. Then: number of free parameters {k}; the nested simpler candidate this one extends (RUN id, {k−n} free parameters) or `starting candidate`; the applicability claimed (condition ranges or regime), compared with the explored ranges in the DATASET axes table.}

## 4. Procedure Settings

{Every setting actually used: iterations, tolerances, seeds, numeric precision, initial values, significance level, solver options. No defaults left implicit.}

## 5. Assumptions

{Each assumption the procedure relies on and what licenses it.}

| Assumption | Licence |
|------------|---------|
| Units of every quantity identical across candidate spec and every dataset in the snapshot | checked against PLAN section 3 concordance on {date} |
| {structural assumption, e.g. a conservation law that removes a state, independence of units, a distribution family} | borrowed: task statement |
| Noise model and its scale | borrowed: simulator config or instrument spec |
| {functional form of a condition dependence, e.g. temperature}, reference point {…} | {DIAG batch that distinguishes it} or `borrowed: {source}` |
| Parameter ranges or priors | `verified: {quote, location}` or `assumed` (an assumed range is reported as such in the verdict notes) |
| {…} | {…} |

## 6. Inputs

{The request payload as sent to the tool: conditions and measurements, or their equivalent for this procedure. Pointer into DATASET provenance (run id, step ids) or the JSON itself when small.}

## 7. Outputs

| Output | Value | Unit | Range or reference | On a limit? |
|--------|-------|------|--------------------|-------------|
| {parameter estimate / statistic / optimum / decision} | {value} | {unit} | [{lo}, {hi}] or {reference} | {yes / no / near} |

{Final objective value as the tool reports it; the agreed quality metric computed exactly as the PLAN defines it, with the reference it is compared against (noise floor, held-out set, reference solution). Where the procedure yields a per-experiment error, the table: experiment, origin, condition, systematic structure yes/no, largest deviation. Parsimony check against the PLAN selection rule: quality of this candidate versus the nested simpler candidate on the same snapshot (difference on the agreed quality metric or information criterion, as the PLAN declares), and for each free parameter added, whether removing it keeps quality within the tie threshold. Then the handoff to the next design, about this candidate only: which hypothesis IDs this RUN supports or falsifies (evidence for the COMPARISON's status updates), which outputs remain poorly determined (candidates for variance-reduction points), and which condition ranges the candidate has not been tested in (candidates for boundary points). Cross-candidate questions belong to the COMPARISON for this snapshot, not here.}

## 8. Deviations

{Experiments excluded; procedure did not converge or terminate normally; limits widened during the phase; phase re-run after human rejection with the feedback text verbatim and what changed. Write `None` explicitly if nothing.}

## 9. Verdict

{One row per criterion declared in the PLAN, in the PLAN's order. No criterion may be added or dropped here. Rows are evaluated top to bottom; the first failing mechanical row stops the evaluation, the rows below it are marked `not evaluated`, and the RUN is not forwarded to review or to human approval. Judged rows are filled by the named human or calibrated judge, never by the agent that produced the RUN.}

| Criterion ID | Measured | Threshold | Measured by | Result | Failure mode |
|--------------|----------|-----------|-------------|--------|--------------|
| `cpt-{system}-criterion-units-match` | {count} | 0 | mechanical | pass / fail | none / biased |
| `cpt-{system}-criterion-budget` | {batches used} | ≤ {budget} | mechanical | pass / fail | none |
| `cpt-{system}-criterion-{quality}` | {value of the agreed quality metric} | {PLAN threshold} | mechanical | pass / fail | none / biased / imprecise |
| `cpt-{system}-criterion-parsimony` | {free parameters removable within tie threshold} | 0 | mechanical | pass / fail | none / imprecise |
| `cpt-{system}-criterion-applicability` | {axes where claim exceeds explored range} | 0 | mechanical | pass / fail | none / biased |
| `cpt-{system}-criterion-checklist` | {count NOT YET TESTED} | 0 | mechanical | pass / fail | none / biased |
| `cpt-{system}-criterion-{…}` | {…} | {…} | {mechanical / judged by: {person}} | pass / fail / not evaluated | {none / biased / imprecise} |

## 10. Reproduction

{The exact tool request JSON or its path; simulator and tool commit; configs. If the simulator is unseeded, say so: the stored measurements are the reference, re-simulation will not reproduce them, re-running the procedure on stored data must reproduce the outputs.}
